title: Harmonize mid-cycle quota adjustments with invoice line alignment
creator: Amelia Zhang
description:
Summary: Mid-cycle quota changes (manual adjustments, plan downgrades, and burst credit reversals) are producing misaligned invoice line items in NetSuite exports. Symptoms include duplicate credit lines, incorrect proration amounts, and reconciliation drift between hour-level usage and monthly invoice lines. This ticket drives changes to the billing export pipeline and proration calculator to ensure deterministic invoice lines for any intra-billing-period allocations.

Reproduction steps: 1) Create customer with monthly quota and hourly metering. 2) Mid-month, apply a quota reduction and issue a manual credit. 3) Trigger billing export. 4) Observe duplicate/fragmented line items in the NetSuite CSV and mismatched Stripe invoice credit vs internal usage.

Expected: Exported invoice lines should consolidate adjustments into parent allocation entries with stable export IDs and clear effective_start/effective_end timestamps so NetSuite can reconcile without duplicate refunds. Proration math should be idempotent across re-runs.

Observed root causes discovered so far: - Billing exporter used allocation timestamps that were updated on subsequent adjustments, causing previously exported line IDs to change. - Proration engine applied rounding per-change rather than at the aggregated allocation level, creating cumulative rounding drift. - Stripe export relied on token-level refunds for quota offsets, while NetSuite required a single consolidated credit row per invoice period.

Proposed approach: 1) Introduce an immutable export_allocation_id (UUID) stamped at first allocation creation and preserved across adjustments. 2) Add effective_start and effective_end to exported rows; exporter will collapse overlapping allocations into a single invoice line during export if same export_allocation_id exists. 3) Perform proration and rounding at aggregated invoice-line granularity (sum then round) instead of per adjustment. 4) Add an export normalization pass that maps Stripe refund events to the consolidated export_allocation_id to avoid duplicate refund rows in NetSuite. 5) Add test coverage for boundary cases: rapid consecutive adjustments, hourly usage spikes, and burst-credit rollbacks.

Out of scope for this ticket: UX for customers, automatic customer notifications (handled in a follow-up), full reprocessing of historical exports beyond 60 days unless finance requests it.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Amelia Z: Spike complete. Confirmed allocation ID mutation is the primary cause. Sample payloads attached in Confluence doc.
2026-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented prototype of immutable export_allocation_id in billing-allocator branch (WIP). See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4219 (draft).

2026-03-02 - Finance (Dana Lewis): Reviewed prototype data. Noted that NetSuite requires consolidated credit rows with memo referencing original invoice number. Added requirement to export invoice_reference in normalization pass.
2026-03-05 - Ravi Singh (PM): Approved approach to aggregate rounding and asked for a canary plan to run exporters for a subset of accounts before full rollout.

2026-03-09 - QA (Sofia Marin): Added test cases in billing-integration suite covering: overlapping adjustments, edge-case rounding on $0.005, and Stripe-to-Netsuite mapping. All tests passing locally.
work_log: 2026-02-22 - Spike: instrumented exporter to log allocation history snapshots for 30 customers (ran for 48h).
2026-02-25 - Dev: added export_allocation_id field and backwards-compatible CSV column to nightly exporter.
2026-03-01 - Dev: changed proration pipeline to compute net_adjustment_per_allocation then round to cents at the end.

2026-03-04 - Integration: normalization pass now emits consolidated credit rows and maps Stripe refund IDs to export_allocation_id. Ran reconciliation on 7 pilot accounts; mismatches reduced from ~12% to <1.5% in those pilots.
2026-03-11 - Canary: scheduled nightly canary for 2% of high-volume accounts starting 2026-03-15. Metrics/alerts defined in Grafana.
acceptance_criteria: Exported NetSuite CSV must include immutable export_allocation_id and effective_start/effective_end columns.
Proration math must round only once after aggregating adjustments for each allocation; existing integration tests must pass.
Finance validation: reconciliation delta between internal usage and exported invoice lines must be < 0.5% for canary cohort.
Canary rollout plan documented and automated rollback in place (exporter feature flag).
Runbook added: manual reconciliation steps and one-off re-export procedure (60-day window).
